notes_list.title: Hofmann Mustard Oil Reaction
notes_list.basic_overview: Primary amines react with carbon disulfide and subsequent reagents to produce isothiocyanates, commonly recognized through the mustard-oil reaction.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
Primary amines can be converted to isothiocyanates, R–N=C=S, which have characteristic pungent mustard-oil odors. The reaction is mainly of qualitative and historical significance in organic identification.

MECHANISM & STEPWISE EXPLANATION
The source describes the transformation as: Primary amines react with carbon disulfide and subsequent reagents to produce isothiocyanates, commonly recognized through the mustard-oil reaction. The mechanism should be read as activation of the stated substrate, formation of the key reactive intermediate, the bond-making/bond-breaking event described by the reaction, and the stated work-up/product-forming step.

1. Activate the stated substrate with the listed reagent/conditions.
2. Generate the key reactive intermediate or electrophile/nucleophile implied by the reaction.
3. Carry out the characteristic bond-forming, bond-breaking or rearrangement step.
4. Complete proton transfer/work-up and verify the characteristic product.
